features.name: markdown_link_share_of_urls
features.definition: Among all link URLs in the counter-argument comments, what proportion are in formatted Markdown links ([text](url)) rather than bare URLs?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads; malformed or missing -> null. Join comments. Markdown links: regex r'\[[^\]]*\]\((https?://[^)\s]+)[^)]*\)' count = m. Remove those matches from the text, then bare URLs: regex r'https?://[^\s<>\)\]]+' count = b. Return m/(m+b); if m+b==0 (including empty list) return null. Raw text matching, no semantic filtering; comment text may contain outcome announcements.

features.name: has_any_url_in_counterarguments
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain any URL, Markdown-formatted or bare?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments JSON; malformed/missing -> null; empty list -> 0. Return 1 if any comment matches r'https?://' else 0.

h0: Among discussions with counter-argument links, the share of URLs that are Markdown-formatted is not associated with delta, controlling for having any URL.
h1: A higher share of Markdown-formatted links (vs. bare URLs) in counter-arguments is associated with higher likelihood of delta.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta. The share feature is null when no URLs exist, so the OLS only uses rows with URLs (patsy drops NaN); the second feature is supplied but not in rhs. Mixed Markdown/bare rows are intermediate shares. Association only; raw text may contain outcome announcements, and comment order/timing is unknown. Regex may miss unusual link syntax (e.g. reference links, angle-bracketed URLs).
